label: Transaction-cost theory of firm boundaries, reading 2 (selection equilibrium)

replace.stanceProfile.evidence (model classes): functional explanation backed by selection (s10), not teleological choice; dynamical because alignment is reached 'over time' (s10).

mechanisms.label: Discriminating alignment as a selection equilibrium: governance varies, misaligned firms bear higher cost and exit, survivors are aligned

assumptions.statement: Economizing is a property of the surviving population: governance structures that are more costly for a transaction do not persist in competitive populations (s1, s10).
Competitive selection is strong and fast enough to eliminate firms that misalign (s10).
Governance arrangements vary across firms, for example through trial, imitation or error, so that selection has variation to act on (surfaced).

propositions.statement: In competitive populations that have had time to be selected, the distribution of governance across transactions approximates discriminating alignment: low asset specificity with market, intermediate with hybrid, high with hierarchy. Individual transactions may be misaligned.
observables: share of aligned transactions by industry

tce:C15.inferentialRole.commitments.statement: If structure g has the lowest governance cost for transaction t, then firms governing t by structures other than g have a lower expected survival (s10).

propositions.statement: The prevalence of misaligned transactions decreases with competitive intensity and with the time a population has been exposed to competition (surfaced from s10 under reading 2).
Among firms of the same age in the same market, misaligned firms have a higher exit hazard than aligned ones (sharpening of P4 under reading 2).
observables: alignment status of the firm's main transactions

scopeConditions.statement: P3 itself (not only P4) holds only in competitive populations observed after selection has had time to act.

openQuestions (added): Under reading 2, P3 does not hold in protected, regulated or young industries. Does the theorist accept that restriction of scope?
Selection acts on firms but alignment is defined per transaction (C16 vs C17.r2). How much misalignment can a firm with many aligned transactions carry before selection bites?
